title: The votes are in, and PC Gamer readers have picked the scariest game on PC

title: 'Are we going too far with this?': One of the worst scenes in Outlast had its devs debating whether to add it to the game or not
summary: How far is too far in a universe that constantly pushes gore to its limits?
body: There are many scenes from Outlast that are burned into my memory, The Groom's sequence in Outlast's Whistleblower DLC, the finger amputation from the first game, or perhaps it was landing on a bunch of baby bones in Outlast 2 . There's quite a lot to pick from over two games, a DLC, and the live service The Outlast Trials . But if Philippe Morin, co-founder of Red Barrels, had to pick the scene that made the team really stop and think about whether this was ok he'd go back to the first game. For those who don't remember, or perhaps have never played the game, or maybe just wiped the encounter from your memory, as the protagonist Miles Upshur is navigating the abandoned Mount Massive Asylum he stumbles across an inmate engaging in necrophilia. It's a pretty startling moment, and was actually the last thing I thought I'd come across, even in an Outlast game. But that was the whole point of that scene. body: المدير الفني الهولندي قاب قوسين أو أدنى من الخروج! تسيطر حالة من الغضب على جماهير الأهلي خلال الساعات الماضية، بعد الخسارة التاريخية التي تعرض لها الفريق أمام الشباب، بنتيجة (1-6)، ضمن منافسات الجولة 12 من بطولة دوري روشن السعودي للمحترفين. وعقب المباراة، واصلت جماهير الأهلي الهجوم على المدرب الهولندي من المدرجات، حيث رددت "بوسيتش أوت" في إشارة لرغبتها في خروجه. اقرأ أيضًا.. رحلة خارجية تكشف حقيقة إقالة بوسيتش من تدريب الأهلي وبحسب ما علم " كووورة " من مصدر مقرب داخل الأهلي، فإن مباراة السد القطري في دوري أبطال آسيا للنخبة، ستكون بمثابة الفرصة الأخيرة في رحلة بوسيتش مع الراقي. ناقش الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة وأوضح المصدر أن أي نتيجة بخلاف الفوز سيغادر بوسيتش منصبه بشكل رسمي على أن يتولى المهمة أحد أبناء النادي بصورة مؤقتة حتى يتم التعاقد مع مدير فني أجنبي خلال الفترة المقبلة. ويحل الأهلي ضيفًا ثقيلًا على السد القطري، مساء الإثنين المقبل، ضمن منافسات الجولة الرابعة من نخبة آسيا. وكان بوسيتش قد هاجم أحد الصحفيين بعد الخسارة أمام الشباب، حيث قال له: "هل سترحل عن الأهلي؟"، ليرد قائلًا: "يجب أن تخجل من نفسك". تذاكر مباريات دوري روشن السعودي اشتر تذكرتك الآن!

body: Anthropic has updated Claude Opus 5.5 to "steer it away" from letting users clone other developers' games, after weeks of Steam being overrun with AI slop and outcries from the game development community. In an update spotted by X user Chasm (via Game Developer ) Anthropic added a new rule to Claude Code's "Rules". Listed under "tengu_heron_brook", the rule reads, "Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user's own designs and assets. Do not build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original." The addition was later confirmed by Addy Osmani, a member of Anthropic's technical staff. In a response to Chasm's post, Osmani stated, "We added two sentences to Claude Code's prompt on Opus 5.5 to steer it away from recreating someone else's specific game because using Claude to infringe IP is against our usage policy." Osmani added that "original games, genre games, and games built from your own design are meant to keep working. We'll continue to iterate to ensure that we're striking the right balance. title: Red Barrels' co-founder is just as confused as we are as to why no one's tried to replicate Outlast's success: 'Honestly, I don't know'
summary: You'd think someone else would've successfully taken gore to the next level.
body: The Outlast series has been providing horror fans with some of the most grotesque and outrageous scenes for 13 years, and to over 50 million players. The most surprising thing about all of that, though, isn't how it's able to keep players terrified, it's that no one else has tried to capitalise on its success. Sure, there've been games which have had their fair share of gore involved, Resident Evil 7 , Harvester, or Agony are just a few that come to mind. But none of them have either managed to top the gore seen in Outlast and also achieve its continued success. (Image credit: Red Barrels) I decided that no one else would be better to ask about this strange phenomenon than Red Barrels' co-founder Philippe Morin, but he seems just as confused as I am that Outlast hasn't had any imitators: "Honestly, I don't know. Sometimes I ask myself the same thing, but I'm glad that we're still different from other games because it can be so hard. There's thousands games coming out on Steam every year. title: I'm 100% here for a more grounded, realistic GTA 6, one I believe won't come at the expense of its usual haphazard chaos
summary: I hope Rockstar makes us work a little harder to wreak our usual mayhem.
body: Edge magazine unleashed a whopper of a 16-page feature all about Grand Theft Auto 6 earlier this week. After poring over every paragraph multiple times, one thing really stuck out to me: It feels like Rockstar is pushing for a more realistic, grounded experience. Those two words might sound like an absolute nightmare to some GTA aficionados. It's not like the series has never known how to be serious or gritty—see Grand Theft Auto 4—but it's always facilitated chaos with relative ease. Outlandish weapons, an easily gamed wanted system, NPCs that feel more like props to be mowed down than anything with a personality. If I wanted to hop in and wreak a little criminal havoc for a while, I wouldn't find much hardship in wriggling out of trouble as soon as I was bored. But it sounds like creating that sort of pandaemonium in GTA 6 is no longer as free as it once was. Police will remember what you looked like, if you were working alone or alongside an accomplice, and any weapon you were carrying. body: Denis Dyack, known for his work on games including Blood Omen: Legacy of Kain and Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem, says big game developers are "abusing early access" by using it as a marketing tool for highly polished games that are ready for full release anyway. That, Dyack believes, has shifted expectations for early access releases overall, and made life more difficult for indie developers who rely on the process to actually get their games finished and launched. "They can put up a polished product and rake in cash," Dyack told GamesIndustry . "It's a marketing beat for them. So, that leaves players often expecting a near-perfect game that, in our opinion, defeats the purpose of early access, which is a collaborative development process based on player feedback. body: In this week's 'what the memory crisis is doing to people' news, a YouTuber has recently bought 32 GB of DDR5 laptop memory online and successfully converted it into memory for their desktop. Overall, it cost them just $175 ($120 for the memory and $55 for extra components). That's a bit of a bargain, as 32 GB DDR5 dual-channel memory is fetching upwards of $500 on Newegg right now. Blighted Agent took to their YouTube channel to share the process, where they purchased two SO-DIMM sticks of 16 GB DDR5 memory on Facebook Marketplace (presumably salvaged from a dead laptop). From here, they put a stick on a preheater, then removed the BIOS chip, the SPD chip and all eight of its memory chips. Buying new DDR5 DIMM PCBs and heatsinks off AliExpress, they cleaned the factory unleaded solder on the laptop memory, then soldered them onto the new PCBs.
